report.source_text: Histological analysis showed proliferation of the chorion in the form of small nests with relatively uniform, medium-sized cells and rounded to polyhedral cells containing homogenous, ovoid nuclei with fine chromatin. It was associated with numerous thin-walled vascular structures, lined by endothelial cells without atypia. The tumour cells containing a cytoplasmic frame well defined by reticulin were positive for actin and caldesmone with low expression for CD99. There was no expression for pancytokeratins, CD34, chromogranin, synaptophysin, S100 protein, SOX-10, desmin or inhibin. There also was no signs of malignancy.

The mass was actively and diffusively bleeding. Haemostasis by electrical bipolar cauterisation was performed, allowing us to control the bleeding; biopsies of the tracheal mass were then performed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An elderly male smoker (early 80s) with a history of hypertension, GERD, and active smoking presented with respiratory distress and massive haemoptysis from a large posterior tracheal mass. Initial endoscopy revealed a bulging, fleshy mass located on the posterior tracheal wall just below the vocal folds, obstructing approximately 90% of the tracheal lumen and extending 2.5 cm distally, with active and diffuse bleeding. Haemostasis was achieved by bipolar cauterisation, and biopsies were obtained. CT imaging confirmed a 25 mm posterior parietal mass in the posterior sub-cricoid trachea with arterial phase contrast uptake and infiltration of the intertracheaoesophageal fat with mass effect on the oesophagus; no distant metastases were identified. Histopathology of the tracheal mass demonstrated proliferation of small nests of uniform, medium-sized cells with rounded to polyhedral nuclei and numerous thin-walled vascular structures lined by endothelial cells without atypia. Immunohistochemical analysis showed positive staining for actin and caldesmone with low CD99 expression, and negative staining for CD34, desmin, chromogranin, synaptophysin, S100, SOX-10, pancytokeratins, and inhibin, with no signs of malignancy. These findings were compatible with glomangioma subtype of glomus tumour. The patient underwent intubation and surgical tracheotomy for airway management. Treatment consisted of volumetric arc therapy radiation at a total dose of 53 Gy over 25 sessions, which was well tolerated without complications. Follow-up endoscopic and radiologic assessments at 3, 6, 9, 12, and 18 months post-radiation demonstrated regression of more than 80% of the tracheal tumour with stability of the minor residual lesion. The patient remained asymptomatic and resumed normal daily activities.
